title: Guest Accounting Principle: One Guest Folio for Each Reservation
content:
**Principle.** A guest may hold any number of Guest Folios, one for each stay; there is no limit on the number of folios one guest holds. Exactly one folio is opened per reservation, at its check-in, and a reservation never has two folios. Each folio is billed, corrected, settled and refunded on its own, and a credit due on one folio is never used to pay another. A folio is opened only for a reservation that does not already have one.

## The principle by element

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Folios per guest | Any number, one for each stay |
| Folios per reservation | Exactly one, opened at check-in |
| Opening a folio | Only for a reservation that does not already have a folio, whatever the status of the existing folio (open, settled or reopened) |
| Billing, corrections, settlement, refunds | Each folio on its own |
| A credit due on one folio | Never used to pay another folio |

The test for opening a folio is made on the system record of the reservation: the reservation behind a folio is the reservation the folio names.

## Basis questions

**A guest has three past stays at Ashbury hotels and a fourth stay is checking in. Is a fourth folio opened?** Yes, if the fourth reservation has no folio yet: one folio per stay, with no cap on the number per guest.

**A reservation already shows a settled folio. May a second folio be opened for the same reservation?** No. A reservation never has two folios, and a settled folio is still that reservation's folio.

**One folio shows a credit due to the guest and another folio of the same guest shows a balance owed. May the credit pay the balance?** No. A credit due on one folio is never used to pay another.
